div.div: One round: a read-only planner sets 2 [I1] bounded tasks, 2 [I2] researchers work in parallel, and only the harness's evaluation worker judges, promotes and writes memory

PLANNER (agent, read-only)
reads champions + lessons + attempts digest; rewrites the lessons; assigns tasks.
May not: modify files, run evaluations, read held-out inputs

TASKS (x 2 [I1])
id, title, parent candidate, hypothesis with numbers from memory, 3-6 steps [I4], success criterion; about 1 hour [I5] each; independent mechanisms

RESEARCHER A (agent)
builds candidates, diagnostics, appends to the worklog; up to 4 submissions [I3]

RESEARCHER B (agent, in parallel)
may not edit the evaluator, an existing candidate, the topic config; may not read held-out

EVALUATION QUEUE
submit blocks until done; one official run at a time

EVALUATION WORKER (harness code, not an agent)
1. paired baseline in the same measurement context, younger than 1440 min [I6]; else run it first
2. re-measure the track's champion if it has no record in this context
3. run the frozen evaluator (diagram 02)
4. apply the promotion policy (diagram 05)
5. write the record and memory

SLOW MEMORY: lessons.md
short (about 70 lines [I7]), curated, every lesson cites a run id; rewritten by the planner each round; negative results KEPT ('X did not help (run id); do not repeat without a new idea')

FAST MEMORY: attempts.jsonl
one row per official evaluation, append-only: candidate, parent, agent, verdict, metric, paired baseline, binding, note. Agents see a digest

champion.json
per track: id, run id, metric, margin, since when, reason, previous champion. Written only by the promotion policy

evidence/<time>-<candidate>/
one directory per run: record, raw outputs, log. The directory name is the run id: 'cite or it did not happen' (B4)

CAPS AND COST (each agent is told its cap, so it reports before it is killed)
- planner: 30 min [I8], 100 credits [I9]; each researcher: 60 min [I10], 300 credits [I11]
- every tool call and credit is recorded; cost per accepted improvement is a campaign metric; a campaign budget pauses the loop
- check the meter in round one: in the demonstration round the agent tool emitted no usage events, so credits read 0 and only the wall-time cap bounded the agents

COORDINATOR (human-facing agent)
commits, writes the weekly report from the records (B8), raises the decisions the policy cannot take. May not: promote by judgement

HUMAN OWNER
owns the evaluator and the promotion rule; decides e.g. whether a near-tie blocked by the rule should change the rule

WHY PAIRED: compare within one measurement context (host, boot, evaluator id), as in blocking in experimental design. In the first campaign absolute latency shifted by 10 % [I14] between two hosts of the same type; an unpaired comparison would have swamped real gains. Demonstration round 1: 4 submissions [I12], 13 min [I13] of wall time.

Legend: green = agent sessions | amber = harness code that judges | blue = files (memory and records) | purple = human-facing | grey = caps | bold arrows = the work path; blue = writes; dashed green = what agents read

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (cited paper, or my arithmetic on public mathematics); [In] = illustrative (a design parameter of the harness, a round value that keeps the shape of the first campaign, or output of the demonstration scheduling simulator; never a measurement of a real platform); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B7-agents-and-the-loop.md (roles table, task shape, queue, paired baseline, champion re-measurement, caps, credit-meter caveat, machine-readable endings); notes/B6-the-two-memories.md (attempts log, lessons file, champions); notes/B4-evidence-records.md (one directory per run, run id); notes/B8-reporting.md (coordinator, weekly report, decisions).
[I1] topic_tasks_per_round = 2 tasks. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I2] topic_researchers_parallel = 2 researchers. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I3] topic_submissions_per_researcher = 4 submissions. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I4] harness_plan_steps = 3-6 steps per task. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I5] harness_task_hours = 1 hour. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I6] topic_baseline_max_age_min = 1440 min. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I7] harness_lessons_max_lines = 70 lines. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I8] topic_planner_wall_min = 30 min. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I9] topic_planner_credits = 100 credits. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I10] topic_researcher_wall_min = 60 min. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I11] topic_researcher_credits = 300 credits. illustrative: configuration of the demonstration topic (design parameter of the harness)
[I12] sched_r1_submissions = 4 submissions. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I13] sched_r1_wall_min = 13 min. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I14] c1_host_shift_illustrative = 10 %. illustrative; keeps the shape of the first campaign (internal methodology notes, 2026), not its values
